name: Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle
description:
The Mitochondrial Depolarization Pulse Rifle operates by projecting a tightly focused beam of modulated electromagnetic radiation tuned to the resonant frequency of cytochrome c oxidase — the terminal enzyme in the mitochondrial electron transport chain. On contact, the beam disrupts proton gradient maintenance across the inner mitochondrial membrane, causing a cascading cellular energy failure in targeted tissue within seconds. The effect is not thermal; cells simply cease producing ATP at the required rate, and motor function collapses from the inside out.

What distinguishes the MDPR-2 from comparable disabling weapons is its selectivity and depth of penetration. The beam attenuates predictably through soft tissue but loses minimal energy through non-biological materials, allowing it to affect targets through light cover such as clothing, padding, or standard-grade ballistic weave. Operators describe the effect on unprotected targets as a progressive 'shutdown' — first peripheral muscle groups, then respiratory muscles if exposure is sustained beyond two seconds. Death is possible but requires deliberate extended trigger hold, which gives the weapon plausible deniability as a compliance tool.

Arcturis Defense Solutions markets the MDPR-2 as a 'non-lethal escalation platform,' though this classification is widely contested by independent biomedical researchers and three separate municipal oversight bodies. The weapon is heavy, requires a dedicated power cell rated for thirty shots, and produces a faint violet corona at the emitter aperture that experienced operators call 'the bruise.' Field technicians note that partial cyberware integration — particularly subdermal power cells — can create unpredictable secondary ionization in the target's implants.
legality: Restricted — licensed to law enforcement and licensed private security contractors only
specifications: effective range: 40 meters optimal, 70 meters degraded effect shots per cell: 30 charge time between shots: 2.1 seconds beam duration for incapacitation: 1.5–2.5 seconds sustained contact weight: 4.8 kg loaded emitter aperture: Tunable — 8cm to 30cm beam spread at 40m secondary hazard: Cyberware interference within 1.5m of beam path
tactical_use: Used primarily for crowd incapacitation, high-value target capture, and facility lockdowns where lethal force creates legal or political liability. Operators are trained to sweep the beam across a target's torso for rapid effect. Extended trigger holds targeting the chest cavity are classified as lethal use and require separate authorization under most jurisdictions. Effective against unaugmented targets and those with organic musculature; heavily augmented individuals with synthetic muscle replacement show reduced susceptibility.
cultural_context: The MDPR-2 has become a symbol of corporate overreach in GLMZ's civil discourse. Footage of security contractors using 'Brownouts' on striking dock workers at the Palladian Construction yard circulated widely on the mesh three years ago, and the weapon is now visually associated with state-adjacent suppression. Activists wear stylized violet corona pins as protest symbols. Conversely, in private security circles, carrying an MDPR-2 signals professionalism and restraint — the idea being that you can stop someone without leaving marks.
story_hooks: A batch of MDPR-2s has gone missing from an Arcturus depot — the serial numbers filed off. Someone is planning to use them at a public event, but the party must determine whether the intent is suppression or assassination.

A character with subdermal power cells was hit by a Brownout and survived — but something in their implants is now cycling incorrectly, and they're experiencing micro-blackouts. The only technician who understands the interaction works for Arcturus.

A corporate whistleblower has evidence that Arcturus has been quietly shipping MDPR-2 units to a government with a documented record of disappearing dissidents. The weapon is legal. The sale is documented. Nothing is technically illegal. That's the problem.

physical_description.visual_profile: A imposing, rifle-form factor with a distinctly medical-scientific aesthetic — all sharp angles and exposed component housing. The emitter dominates the forward profile, a textured cylindrical aperture ringed with concentric cooling fins. The receiver is modular and slightly asymmetrical, suggesting tool-swappable internal architecture. Overall impression is clinical precision weaponized: something designed in a biotech lab rather than an armory.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 118 cm overall | Barrel/emitter: 34 cm | Width at receiver: 9 cm | Depth at stock: 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and substantial — 4.8 kg loaded — with weight distributed forward toward the emitter assembly. Feels anchored and deliberate in hand; not unwieldy but demanding respect from smaller-framed operators. The balance point sits slightly ahead of the trigger guard.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite (body/stock), anodized aluminum receiver housing, surgical-grade stainless steel emitter assembly with copper alloy heat-sink fins
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray on polymer, brushed aluminum on receiver with light oxidation marks, polished stainless on emitter aperture. Heat-stress discoloration (faint purple-bronze patina) visible on fin edges where violet corona bleeds during sustained operation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant: steely gray-blue | Accents: brushed silver, burnt copper on heat fins, faint violet at emitter mouth (when powered) | Trim: black polymer grip and rail sections
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with crosshatch texture for secure purchase even in wet conditions. Grip wraps both pistol grip and forward rail section. Warm to the touch under normal conditions; develops heat signature under sustained fire.
distinctive_features: Concentric copper alloy cooling fins surrounding emitter aperture — visually distinctive, functionally necessary for repeated discharge
Modular rail system along entire top and sides — suggests aftermarket optics, power taps, secondary emitters
Violet corona glow at emitter aperture when powered but not firing — the 'bruise' operators reference
Digital readout on right side of receiver displaying charge state, shot count, and frequency tuning
Recessed access panel on stock hiding dedicated power cell bay — Iron Point branding stamped in serif font
Subtle asymmetry in cooling fin arrangement — left side vents more densely than right, suggesting heat pathway optimization
Worn score marks and grip tape patches on aftermarket examples — evidence of field modification and intensive use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Iron Point Ammunition logo (stylized point within circle) stamped on left side of receiver in 2cm height | Serial plate on stock in white-on-black industrial font | Small biomedical warning symbol (mitochondrion outline) above trigger guard | Frequency tuning range specifications etched along barrel shroud in tiny numerics
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn examples show scuffed matte finish, worn grip tape, minor heat-stress discoloration on fins, and accumulated dust in cooling assembly. Well-maintained contractor weapons appear nearly pristine except for micro-abrasions around emitter from frequent lens cleaning. Heavily deployed units show charred polymer on grip from repeated charging cycles and visible copper oxidation bloom on fins.
